classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate reciprocal composite functions, solve for zero gradient and substitute to obtain coordinates.

content.prompt: Differentiate and find coordinates of any points where the tangent is horizontal.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(1+x^2)^{-1}\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=-1(1+x^2)^{-2}(2x)\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=-2x(1+x^2)^{-2}\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2x}{(1+x^2)^2}\end{align*}$$
A horizontal tangent has gradient $0$. Since $(1+x^2)^2>0$,
$$\begin{align*}-2x&=0\\x&=0\\y&=\frac{1}{1+0^2}\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
The point is $(0,1)$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-3(x^4-2x^2-1)^{-1}\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=-3(-1)(x^4-2x^2-1)^{-2}\\&\qquad\times(4x^3-4x)\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=12x(x^2-1)(x^4-2x^2-1)^{-2}\\\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{12x(x^2-1)}{(x^4-2x^2-1)^2}\end{align*}$$
A horizontal tangent has gradient $0$. Where the function is defined,
$$\begin{align*}12x(x^2-1)&=0\\12x(x-1)(x+1)&=0\\x&=0,\ 1,\ -1\end{align*}$$
All three values give nonzero denominators.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=-\frac{3}{-1}=3\\y(1)&=-\frac{3}{1-2-1}=\frac32\\y(-1)&=-\frac{3}{1-2-1}=\frac32\end{align*}$$
The points are $(0,3)$, $(1,\tfrac32)$ and $(-1,\tfrac32)$.
